clue.text: Swede gives you wind? Then take a very little!

parts.note: a gust is a sudden blast of wind
v is the little, shortened form of very, as in v. good

explanation.surface: A joke about a Swede's flatulence, followed by advice to take only a tiny dose of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swede' suggests the vegetable and its effect on the digestion, but it is a man: Gustav is a common Swedish name, borne by several Swedish kings.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav is a typical Swedish forename, carried by several kings of Sweden, so a Swede may bear it.

clue.text: Person incarcerated, having upset one pope

definitions.text: Person incarcerated, having upset one pope

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset turns the convict's word bottom to top

parts.note: an old lag is a convict serving time in prison
the Roman numeral for one is I
Leo is the name of thirteen popes

explanation.surface: A prisoner whose confinement followed a quarrel with a pontiff.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the astronomer was confined after his writings offended Pope Urban VIII.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian astronomer spent his last years under house arrest after the Inquisition condemned his heliocentric views.

clue.text: Wife, perhaps, makes never-ending protest

indicators.note: the protest word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to squawk is to complain loudly

explanation.surface: A married woman makes an endless fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: An old, now offensive, term for a Native American woman or wife; perhaps flags it as one kind of wife.

clue.text: I transfer property and I learn somehow to keep nothing

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold another letter within them
the letters of I and learn are put together in some new way

parts.note: zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone describes a property deal and a puzzling lesson about keeping nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: In law an alienor is the party who transfers ownership of property to another, the speaker of the definition.

clue.text: Secret revealed by miss in court

indicators.note: the word for miss is placed within the court abbreviation

parts.note: to lose a chance is to miss it

explanation.surface: A secret comes out because a young woman appears in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miss' looks like a young woman, but it is a verb meaning fail to catch.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective closet means kept hidden, as in a closet supporter, which is secret.

clue.text: Maria getting parts the wrong way round, beginning to astound her fans herein?

definitions.text: Maria getting parts the wrong way round, beginning to astound her fans herein?

indicators.note: the name is split into two parts, which then swap places

parts.note: Maria Callas, the celebrated operatic soprano

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A diva gets her lines muddled yet still thrills her audience in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts the wrong way round' splits the name in two and swaps the halves. Callas, the great soprano, sang many famous roles at Milan's opera house.
explanation.definitionFit: Milan's opera house was where Callas triumphed, so it is the place where she astounded her admirers.

clue.text: Keep a close eye on little chap having port

parts.note: Stan is a little, shortened form of the name Stanley
Dover is the English Channel ferry port in Kent

explanation.surface: Someone told to watch a small man who owns a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little chap' suggests a small boy, but it is a shortened name.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand over someone is to supervise them closely, watching every move they make.

clue.text: It's dull outside, possibly

indicators.note: suggests the letters of outside might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A remark that the weather out of doors may be grey.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedious means boring and wearisome, a common synonym of dull.

clue.text: A million-million-millionth of a tropical tree?

parts.note: the indefinite article, written an before a vowel
atto- is the metric prefix for ten to the minus eighteen

explanation.surface: A question about an unimaginably tiny fraction of a tree in the tropics.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatto, more often spelt annatto, is a small tropical American tree whose seeds give an orange dye.

clue.text: Various components from USA installed in a volcanic archipelago near Alaska

indicators.note: the letters are taken in various different orders, signalling rearrangement

explanation.surface: Assorted American-made parts fitted into a chain of volcanic islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' looks like the link into the definition, but both words are part of the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This chain of volcanic islands stretches west from the Alaska Peninsula, separating the Bering Sea from the Pacific.

clue.text: Suddenly appear depressed, being treated like rubbish?

indicators.note: the word for depressed is dealt with as rubbish is, by being put in the bin

parts.note: a bin is where rubbish goes
low means sad or depressed

explanation.surface: Someone feels down because others treat them as worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being treated like rubbish' reads as a description of someone, but it says the depressed word is binned, put inside the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow in is an informal idiom for arriving unexpectedly or casually, which is to suddenly appear.

clue.text: Cross section surveyed about opening feature

indicators.note: the pieces are looked at back to front, read from the other end

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix, especially in a church
a part is a section of something

explanation.surface: An angry surveyor examines a cross-section of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective meaning angry, but it is the rood.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatch in a floor or ceiling is a feature that opens, letting people pass through.

clue.text: I love to follow hussy cycling round? Quite possibly

definitions.text: I love to follow hussy cycling round? Quite possibly

indicators.note: the next pieces come after the hussy word
the letters of the word for hussy move round from the front to the back

parts.note: a harlot is a promiscuous woman, a hussy
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to chasing a flighty woman around on a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: HARLOT cycled becomes LOTHAR, with I and O added. A seducer could quite possibly say the whole clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lothario is a heartless seducer of women, named from a character in Rowe's play The Fair Penitent.

clue.text: What's reduced pain for the French? Nothing could be worse!

definitions.text: What's reduced pain for the French? Nothing could be worse!

parts.words: What's reduced pain for the French? Nothing could be worse!
parts.note: pain is French for bread, so a reduced amount of it is a partial portion, which the proverb says beats having no bread at all

explanation.surface: A question about pain relief in France with an exclamation of dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pain' is French for bread; the proverb says this is better than no bread.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that a partial portion of bread beats none, so settling for part of something beats nothing.

clue.text: Recommend genius finally spotted in commercial contest

parts.note: an ad is a television commercial

indicators.note: the letter is seen inside the word for contest

parts.note: to vie is to compete or contest

indicators.note: only the last letter of genius is taken

explanation.surface: A brilliant person is noticed in an advertising competition and recommended.
explanation.definitionFit: To advise someone is to recommend a course of action to them.

clue.text: Program gives computer company trouble initially

parts.note: Apple is the computer maker

indicators.note: the first letter of trouble is taken

explanation.surface: Software causes problems for a computer firm at first.
explanation.definitionFit: An applet is a small computer program, typically one that runs within another application.

clue.text: Something to soothe old boy turning up after a scene

indicators.note: the turned piece comes after the scene word

parts.note: a scene is a place where something happens

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up reverses the letters bottom to top

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A former pupil appears at the scene to calm things down.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy pill given to please or soothe a patient rather than to cure.

clue.text: Temptation to keep quiet — it helps the digestion

indicators.note: the temptation phrase holds a letter within it

parts.note: temptation is a prompting to try sin
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: Temptation should be kept silent, a remark about something good for the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Trypsin is a digestive enzyme secreted by the pancreas, breaking down proteins in the small intestine.

clue.text: PM no longer having it — end of story?

definitions.text: PM no longer having it — end of story?

parts.note: John Major is a former British prime minister

indicators.note: only the last letter of story is taken

explanation.surface: A prime minister loses his grip on power and his tale is over.
explanation.walkthrough: John Major, British prime minister 1990 to 1997, lost his majority, so the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A majority is what a governing prime minister needs in Parliament; once lost, the story of office ends.

clue.text: Like a sort of finish with performer of farce in bed

parts.note: mat or matt describes a dull, non-glossy finish
Brian Rix was a British actor famous for Whitehall farces

explanation.surface: A dull surface and a farceur caught in bed together.
explanation.walkthrough: Brian Rix starred in British stage farces in which characters were often caught in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology and biology a matrix is the bed of material in which something is embedded.

clue.text: Is it just like Mick to provide sugar?

parts.note: Mick Jagger, singer of the Rolling Stones
the suffix -y makes an adjective meaning like or resembling

explanation.surface: A question whether a rock star's manner can sweeten things.
explanation.walkthrough: Mick Jagger plus -y gives something like Mick.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaggery is a coarse brown sugar made from palm sap or sugar cane in South Asia.

clue.text: We'd hear from Spooner that it's important to get hold of food in the afternoon

indicators.note: the clergyman known for swapping the opening sounds of words gives his version

parts.note: key means crucial or important
to take something is to get hold of it

explanation.surface: The Reverend Spooner advises grabbing something for afternoon tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacake is a sweet currant bun, toasted and buttered, eaten at afternoon tea.

clue.text: Animal psychiatrist not an aid to bring about change

parts.note: a cat is an animal

indicators.note: the following little word is left out of the psychiatrist's title

parts.note: an analyst is a psychoanalyst or psychiatrist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pet therapist is no help in making people change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not an aid' reads as a phrase, but 'not an' tells you to drop AN from ANALYST.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalyst is something that speeds up or brings about a change, in chemistry or in life.

clue.text: Silly talk by a so-called "Dubya" makes one laugh

parts.note: guff is empty, foolish talk
Dubya is the nickname of George W Bush, from how a Texan says his middle initial

explanation.surface: Nonsense from George W Bush makes someone burst out laughing.
explanation.definitionFit: A guffaw is a loud, hearty laugh.

clue.text: A shrub or trees, might you say?

indicators.note: asks whether the word for trees spoken out loud would match

parts.note: firs are coniferous trees

explanation.surface: A question whether a plant should be called a bush or a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Furze, also called gorse, is a spiny yellow-flowered evergreen shrub.

clue.text: Modern achievers out to becoming "topping" in the West Country

indicators.note: the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Contemporary high-flyers aspire to become the elite of south-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Country is south-west England; this rich clotted cream tops scones at a cream tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Clotted cream from Devon is spread on scones, a topping, in south-west England.

clue.text: Sin away before death

indicators.note: the away word comes before the death word

parts.note: off means away, as in go off
one's end is one's death

explanation.surface: Wrongdoing is gone before dying.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend is to sin, to transgress a moral or divine law.

clue.text: Fantastic scenery: when sun comes out, see the old city

indicators.note: the letters of scenery are made into something fantastic, a new arrangement

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for sun or Sunday

explanation.surface: Gorgeous views once the sun breaks out, a chance to see an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: Take S out of SCENERY to leave CENERY, then rearrange. 'comes out' here means removed, not emerges.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyrene was an ancient Greek city in what is now Libya.
